description: AVPx Dedicated Server: puts one commit of the Java server on this machine, only if its jars are the ones the gates tested (deploy/remote-deploy.sh). Made by deploy/make-ssm-document.sh; never edit by hand.

commit.description: The commit to put in place: 40 hex digits, small letters.

jarsSha256.description: The SHA-256 of what sha256sum avpx-server.jar avpx-smoke.jar prints, for the jars the gates built and tested for that commit: 64 hex digits, small letters.

runCommand: # Puts one commit of the server on this machine, or leaves the one already there. Written 2026-11-09 by Melanikus for AVPx Dedicated
# Run as root by the SSM document avpx-deploy (deploy/avpx-deploy.ssm.json, made from this file by deploy/make-ssm-document.sh), which
# GitHub's deploy workflow asks AWS to run once the user has approved it. Nobody logs in to do this.
# WHAT IT DOES, in order, stopping at the first thing that fails:
#   1. checks its two values again: the commit is 40 hex digits, the jars' sha256 64;
#   2. fetches the source of exactly that commit from GitHub, over HTTPS, and unpacks it;
#   3. builds the jar there with the pinned JDK (java/build.sh, which also runs the tests);
#   4. checks both jars, the server (avpx-server.jar) and its smoke test (avpx-smoke.jar), are byte for byte the ones the gates built and
#      tested. What it's given is the SHA-256 of what `sha256sum avpx-server.jar avpx-smoke.jar` prints in the build folder, the same
#      on both sides. The build is the same every time (java.yml checks that), so a different value means something differs, and nothing
#      is put in place. The smoke jar runs as root here, as the health check, so it must be the tested one as much as the server;
#   5. puts it in /opt/avpx/releases/<commit>, and moves the /opt/avpx/current link to it in one step;
#   6. restarts the service, and checks it's healthy (section HEALTH below);
#   7. if anything from step 5 on fails, moves the link back to the release before, restarts that, and fails.
# The settings (/etc/avpx/settings.json) and the certificate are never touched: only /opt/avpx changes.
# AVPX_DEPLOY_ROOT: only deploy/test-remote-deploy.sh sets it, to a folder that stands in for /, so every step can be tested with no
# machine. On a real machine it's never set.
# 1. The two values, checked again here: the SSM document checks them too, but this script trusts nothing it's given
[ "$#" -eq 2 ] || refuse "give exactly the commit and the jars' sha256"
case "$commit" in *[!0-9a-f]*) refuse 'the commit must be 40 hex digits, small letters' ;; esac
case "$want" in *[!0-9a-f]*) refuse "the jars' sha256 must be 64 hex digits, small letters" ;; esac
[ "${#commit}" -eq 40 ] || refuse 'the commit must be 40 hex digits, small letters'
[ "${#want}" -eq 64 ] || refuse "the jars' sha256 must be 64 hex digits, small letters"
# 2. The source of exactly that commit
[ -d "$tree" ] || refuse "the source didn't unpack into a folder named for $commit"
# 3. The build, with the pinned JDK
JAVA_HOME="$jdk" sh "$tree/java/build.sh" > "$work/build.log" 2>&1 || { tail -n 20 "$work/build.log"; refuse 'the build or its tests failed'; }
# 4. The very jars the gates tested: the SHA-256 of what sha256sum prints for both, in the build folder
jars_sha() { (cd "$1" && sha256sum avpx-server.jar avpx-smoke.jar) | sha256sum | cut -d ' ' -f 1; }
[ "$got" = "$want" ] || refuse "the jars built here ($got) aren't the ones the gates built and tested ($want); nothing was put in place"
# 5. In place, and the link moved in one step (a new link, then renamed over the old)
[ "$(jars_sha "$release")" = "$want" ] || refuse "$release is there already, with another jar"
# HEALTH: the service runs, and the smoke test passes against it. With --installed (java/tools/Smoke.java), it reads
# /etc/avpx/settings.json, talks to 127.0.0.1 only on the settings' ports, trusts only the certificate the settings name, runs its 32
# checks, and changes nothing that stays: its one room is closed and its one listing (network version 65535, which no game uses) taken
say "$commit is in place, and healthy"
say "$commit isn't healthy: going back to $before"
healthy && say 'the release before is back, and healthy' || say 'THE RELEASE BEFORE IS BACK, BUT NOT HEALTHY EITHER'
say "$commit isn't healthy, and there's no release before it to go back to"
